extracted.intended_audience: ICML 2026 reviewers, area chairs, program chairs, and submitting authors (participants in the ICML 2026 peer-review process)
extracted.subtask_description: Conference-level policy specifying permitted and prohibited use of large language models (LLMs) during ICML 2026 peer review, plus matching, visibility, enforcement, and example workflows. Applies to reviewers, meta-reviewers, area chairs, program chairs, and authors who choose policy preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-policy framework (Policy A and Policy B)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICML 2026 will follow a two-policy framework for LLM use in reviewing, consisting of Policy A (Conservative) and Policy B (Permissive). Reviewers declare which policy they want to follow, authors declare whether they require Policy A or allow Policy B, and submissions are matched with compatible reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework is designed to balance retaining human assessment, meeting reviewers where they are in tool use, respecting authors who opt out, and upholding integrity and transparency. Full details (matching, enforcement, visibility) are specified elsewhere in the policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy A (Conservative) — prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of LLMs in any stage of reviewing is strictly prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: inadvertent use in tools that are not traditionally LLM-based, like web search/retrieval and spelling/grammar checkers, is allowed. Reviewers who are assigned or require Policy A must not use LLMs beyond those narrow exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy B (Permissive) — allowed uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed: Use of LLMs to help understand the paper and related works, and polish reviews. Submissions can be fed to privacy-compliant LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific allowed actions (in Appendix/examples): feed submission into a privacy-compliant LLM; ask clarifying questions about the submission; ask about background concepts or concepts introduced earlier in the paper; ask LLM to help retrieve related works and identify connections/overlaps; use LLM to help polish the final review. Use of LLMs is intended to support understanding and polishing, not to delegate judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy B (Permissive) — prohibited uses (delegation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not allowed: Delegation of judgement and critique of the paper to LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly includes asking LLMs to assess paper quality/significance; identify strengths/weaknesses; suggest key points for the review; suggest an outline for the review; write the full review; or suggest questions for authors. Also, feeding submissions to non-privacy-compliant LLMs is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy-compliant LLMs definition
rubrics_metrics.description: By 'privacy-compliant', the policy refers to LLM tools that do not use logged data for training and that place limits on data retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include enterprise/institutional subscriptions to LLM APIs, consumer subscriptions with an explicit opt-out from training, and self-hosted LLMs. The policy notes this is an oversimplification and not an exhaustive legal definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibility and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Under both policies, reviewers are always responsible for the full content of their reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any hallucinated content in reviews is subject to disciplinary action according to the academic integrity policy. Low-quality reviews may result in penalties according to the reciprocal reviewing policy. Reviewers must ensure content accuracy and originality regardless of AI assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are expected to read the entire body of the paper, but not necessarily appendices and supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies under both policies and reinforces that reviewers should form judgments based on their own reading of the paper's main body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer and author declarations (matching input)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers declare which policy they want to follow; authors declare whether they require Policy A or allow Policy B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These declarations are used in the matching process so that papers requiring A are reviewed only by reviewers with Actual Policy A, while papers that allow B may be reviewed by a mix of Actual Policy A and B reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual Policy assignment and matching algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer is explicitly told a single policy they must follow on all of their assigned papers (their Actual Policy). Reviewers who prefer Policy A will be assigned Actual Policy A. Reviewers who prefer B might be assigned Actual Policy A or B; the matching algorithm will try to minimize overrides from B to A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers that require A will be reviewed by reviewers with Actual Policy A. Papers that allow B will be reviewed by reviewers some of whom have Actual Policy A and some Actual Policy B. Matching ensures compatibility and tries to respect reviewer preferences where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity requirement for reviewers who are authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reviewer who is also an author of a paper that requires Policy A must also be willing to follow Policy A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enforces fairness so authors who require conservative reviewing cannot be reviewed by reviewers who will not abide by the same constraints on their own submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility and privacy of policy choices
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy chosen by each paper is only visible to the authors of that paper, but not to the reviewers or meta-reviewers, and will not be published in the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy preference and Actual Policy of each reviewer are only visible to that reviewer, but not to the authors, other reviewers, or meta-reviewers. This limits potential strategic behavior and preserves confidentiality of choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization and monitoring (experimental evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program chairs may randomize some Actual Policy assignments within constraints to (1) monitor differences between distributions of scores given by Actual Policy A and B reviewers and (2) run an experiment to evaluate outcome differences between the policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If systematic differences are identified, chairs will act to compensate. Collected data will be analyzed to inform future policies and results might be published in a peer-reviewed publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and consequences for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are required to strictly follow their assigned Actual Policy when reviewing and discussing papers. Any attempt to deviate constitutes a violation of the academic integrity policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations may result in actions by program chairs, including desk rejection of the reviewer's own submissions and other disciplinary measures per the academic integrity policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: concrete allowed actions under Policy B
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples of allowed behaviors when following Policy B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed: Feed submission into privacy-compliant LLM; ask clarifying questions about the submission; ask about background concepts or concepts introduced earlier; ask LLM to help retrieve related works and identify connections/overlaps; use LLM to help polish the final review. The appendix provides an 'Example workflow' illustrating how to combine self-reading with LLM assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: concrete prohibited actions under Policy B
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples of prohibited behaviors under Policy B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not allowed: Feed submission into an LLM that is not privacy-compliant; ask LLM to summarize the paper; ask LLM to evaluate strengths and weaknesses; ask LLM to write a review; ask LLM to suggest questions for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example workflow when following Policy B
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested step-by-step workflow integrating LLM assistance under Policy B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Feed submission into a privacy-compliant LLM. 2) Read the paper yourself, using the LLM for clarifying questions about mathematical concepts and related-work connections. 3) Use the LLM to explore related work. 4) Outside the LLM, write the paper summary (possibly bullets), formulate strengths and weaknesses, formulate overall judgment and the three major supporting reasons, and formulate clarification questions for authors. 5) Use the LLM to polish the final review and questions, keeping things concise and watching for embellishments and hallucinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles of policy design
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy is designed to retain human assessment as crucial, meet reviewers where they are in AI usage, respect authors' preferences about LLM use, and uphold integrity and transparency of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles shaped the two-policy framework and the balance between conservative and permissive options, and inform monitoring, enforcement, and matching decisions.
